diagnostic_browser_cases.scope: JavaScript diagnostic start ordering after applied layout/completed receive callback and cancellation by a newer bootstrap. An assetProbe report is an ordering observation; these cases do not assert that every asset subprobe succeeded and do not prove native custom-origin support, Swift readiness or installed resource identity.

capture_review.method: Direct visual inspection of the eight downloaded, hash-verified PNGs listed below; images were not edited or regenerated.
observations: The overview shows the board, oval track, train, buildings, trees and pond with readable primary controls. No obvious missing scene or overlapping primary control is visible in this inspected frame.
The restored night frame shows Cedar crossing, Saved on this device, the selected Night control and 0 mm/s. It retains the visible train and scenery.

The recovery before/after pair retains the same visible scene and broad lighting appearance; the after frame reads The railway is ready again. This visual observation does not establish pixel identity.
The supplementary joint image renders all four labeled panels. The visible central rail profiles have no obvious gap at this image resolution; close-up endpoints are outside the frame.
The upper case lid remains cropped in the overview and recovery framing. These images are bounded desktop regression evidence, not final art approval or a full inspection of all 23 captures.

The actual 358×300 maximum-name capture shows dark title text on a light backing with single-line ellipsis. The backing remains within the frame and visibly clears the lighting and camera controls. The image alone does not expose the full 80-character accessible name.

The actual 382×575 maximum-name capture shows the title on a light panel with two-line truncation and visible separation from the adjacent lighting controls. The overline and secondary heading text remain visible; no overlap between the title backing and those controls is apparent.

The actual 430×900 night-portrait capture shows Alpine afternoon in light text on the dark green title backing, visibly separated from the rendered case and clear of the adjacent lighting and camera controls. This is a visual observation of the retained frame, not a measured native contrast or accessibility result.

In the narrow daytime captures, the separate status/caption text still crosses the rendered scene. This title-backing review does not certify that separate readability area or all text over all camera positions.
capture_review.scope: Actual desktop Chromium/SwiftShader captures only; no physical-device, motion quality, native accessibility, production-seam or owner-approval conclusion.

acceptance_boundary.reason: Actual native integration, complete required workflow review and coordinator acceptance remain separate. This record does not change project state or establish App Store readiness.
